subject: Post-call: Context & output profile for pricing (8k / 32k / 128k needs)
snippet: Recap of token mix, context window distribution and preliminary $/1M target; next steps for pilot and SE deep-dive.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Context & output profile for pricing (8k / 32k / 128k needs)

Alex — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a tailored pricing and pilot proposal.

Summary from our conversation:
- Product: FinTechX conversational insights for account aggregation and dispute summarization.
- Current volume (estimated): ~15M tokens/month today; growth to 50–75M tokens/month in 6–9 months depending on pilot.
- Goals: keep unit economics near your target (~$600 / 1M tokens) while preserving latency for synchronous flows.

Data/profile requests (can be rough):
1) Avg prompt tokens per request (today): ?
2) Avg completion tokens per request (today): ?
3) Distribution across context-window needs: roughly what percent of calls need >8k, >32k, >128k context?
4) Any hard compliance notes (PII redaction, retention) beyond SOC2?

What we'll do with this: our pricing scenarios model three profiles (8k-first, 32k-mixed, 128k-sparse) and compute spend at your volume bands plus a $/1M token sensitivity table.

Attached: please drop a small sample CSV with rows like: request_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, context_length_required (approx). That will let our SE run a quick simulated cost / latency profile.

Proposed next steps:
- You reply with the sample CSV (or a short summary of the averages / distribution).
- We will return: (A) a 30-day pilot plan with expected spend and SLOs, (B) unit economics at your target $/1M and a suggested cost-saving config (batching + KV caching + quantized model suggestion).

Thanks — will loop in Karthik for a short pricing walkthrough once we have the sample.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ftx_token_samples.csv (sample rows), redwood_pricing_estimate_v1.pdf (placeholder)

From: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Lee <dana.engineering@fintechx.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Context & output profile for pricing (8k / 32k / 128k needs)

Marissa — thanks, appreciate the clear asks. Attached a quick export and a short note from Dana (engineering) with the empirical numbers based on a 30k-sample. See highlights below.

Highlights from our telemetry (30k samples):
- Avg prompt tokens: 420 (median 320).
- Avg completion tokens: 930 (median 700).
- Token mix: 72% of requests have context <= 8k; 22% require context between 8k-32k; 6% hit >32k and of that ~1% require near-128k (very long account histories).
- Peak concurrency: 120 rps for synchronous flows; background batch jobs add ~30% during EOD windows.
- Monthly projected volume for pilot: 15M tokens (month 1), scaling to 40M tokens by month 6 if pilot succeeds.
- Budget target: internal procurement wants to see prices targeting ~$600 per 1M tokens or lower for sustained usage; can tolerate higher in month-1 pilot.

Compliance notes: SOC2 in place; PII redaction is partially handled client-side today, want to discuss retention and customer-managed keys later.

Attached file: ftx_token_samples.csv (first 10 rows), includes fields: request_id,prompt_tokens,completion_tokens,context_tokens_estimate.

Happy to jump on a short SE call to review how you model batching and KV caching impact on unit cost.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Integrations
FinTechX

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Context & output profile for pricing (8k / 32k / 128k needs)

Appreciate the quick data, Alex — this is exactly what we needed. I ran the sample through our SE cost-sim (high level) and pulled two conservative scenarios to align with your $/1M target and show trade-offs.

Scenario A — latency-first (synchronous flows prioritized)
- Model: Redwood-Large (8k optimized kernel), with prefix caching enabled for repeated account-context lookups.
- Effective unit price (simulated): $680 / 1M tokens at 15M tokens/mo (pilot).
- Expected monthly spend (15M): ~$10,200.
- Notes: good latency; 22% of requests (>8k but <=32k) would fall back to a 32k variant with marginally higher token cost for those calls.

Scenario B — cost-first (batching + 32k routing)
- Model: Redwood-Medium-32k variant, batching windows up to 50ms for non-critical flows.
- Effective unit price (simulated): $540 / 1M tokens at 15M tokens/mo.
- Expected monthly spend (15M): ~$8,100.
- Notes: ~5–7% added tail latency for synchronous endpoints; best for summary/batch flows.

128k profile: With your ~1% 128k-class calls, we recommend a separate rarer-exec path (on-demand 128k worker) instead of routing all traffic to 128k. We model that at an incremental premium per 1M for that bucket — given volumes, expected incremental spend is small (~+$250–$500/mo at pilot scale).

Unit economics table (pilot 15M tokens):
- Your target: $600 / 1M tokens -> pilot spend = $9,000/mo.
- Scenario A above = $10.2k/mo (slightly above target).
- Scenario B above = $8.1k/mo (below target).

Recommended immediate next steps:
1) Approve a 30-day pilot at Scenario B pricing with a limited SLO for synchronous endpoints (we can set strict fallbacks).
2) SE deep-dive: Karthik can run a 1-hour sim with your sample CSV and tune batching/caching to validate the $/1M result.
3) If you want, we can stage a canary: route 5% of traffic to Redwood-32k variant and measure latency/quality for 7 days before widening.

If that sounds good, Alex, I’ll draft a one-page pilot statement of work and rough PO-level estimate for procurement.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
